objectives: Situate Olympic breaking + AI choreography in the field.
Reason about climate + global commissioning + the choreographer's 2026 horizon.

slides.title: Viral dance — TikTok, the Renegade + algorithmic visibility
slides.body:
By the mid-2010s, **social-media platforms** became the largest-audience dance distribution channels in human history. **TikTok** (ByteDance; launched outside China 2018; merged with Musical.ly 2018) is the dominant force: vertical 9:16 video, 15-60 second clips, an algorithmic recommendation feed that surfaces dances to non-followers of the creator, a music + sound library that lets any user attach a viral track to their own video. Dance + TikTok have a mutually-shaping relationship: dances spread the platform + the platform reshapes the dances.

**The Renegade case study (2019-2020)**. **Jalaiah Harmon** (14, Atlanta) created a complex 14-step choreography to K Camp's *Lottery (Renegade)* in September 2019 + posted it to Funimate + Instagram. The dance — combining hip-hop arm work, isolations, the 'wave', 'whoa', the 'wide leg' — spread to TikTok where **Charli D'Amelio** (then 15) posted it without credit + accumulated ~100M views; for months Harmon went uncredited as the choreographer + did not benefit financially from the virality. The story broke in the *New York Times* (February 2020, Taylor Lorenz) + became the canonical case for *uncredited Black creators of viral choreography* + the resulting industry push for credit + compensation reform. Harmon was later named to the *Time* 100 + signed by major agencies. **The Renegade lesson**: TikTok + Instagram virality decouple choreography from its author + from compensation.

**WAP + Brian Esperon (2020)**. **Brian Esperon** (Guam-based choreographer) choreographed the dance for Cardi B + Megan Thee Stallion's *WAP* (August 2020); the routine — split-pop, mat work, knee slides, full body waves — became one of the most-replicated TikTok dances of the year + a discourse object on agency + sexuality + Black + Latina women's choreography. Esperon was credited from the start, a partial correction to the *Renegade* pattern.

**Algorithmic visibility**. The TikTok algorithm rewards (a) **early completion + replay**, (b) **stitches, duets + downloads**, (c) **sound reuse**, (d) **trending hashtags**. A choreographer for TikTok designs an 8-count hook that is (i) learnable in 60 seconds; (ii) instagrammable from a fixed phone tripod; (iii) attached to a sound that pulls viewers + creators. The *Savage* dance (Keara Wilson 2020 to Megan Thee Stallion), the *Say So* dance (Haley Sharpe 2020 to Doja Cat), the *Megan Thee Stallion Hot Girl Summer* + dozens of others followed.

**Tensions**:
- **Credit** + **compensation** — TikTok pays sound owners but typically not choreographers; reforms are slow.
- **Cultural appropriation** — Black + Latino vernacular dance circulating uncredited.
- **Body image + mental health** — dance virality pressures on adolescent creators.
- **Choreography-as-content** versus choreography-as-art — TikTok pulls dance toward replicable hooks + away from long-form composition (P89 L3).

**Concert + commercial choreographers** now have to decide whether + how to use TikTok as a distribution + recruitment channel + how to credit + license viral choreography. The platform has become a structural fact of the field.

slides.title: Olympic breaking + concert-AI hybrids — Wayne McGregor + Random International
slides.body:
**Breaking at Paris 2024**. **Breaking** (b-boying / b-girling — Bronx, early 1970s; P89 L6) was added to the **Paris 2024 Summer Olympics** as a medal sport. Olympic format: 1v1 battle rounds, 60 seconds each, judged on technique + variety + execution + musicality + creativity (the OBJ scoring system co-developed with the World DanceSport Federation). Gold medalists: **Ami** (Yuasa Ami, Japan) in B-girls; **Phil Wizard** (Phil Kim, Canada) in B-boys. The inclusion polarised the global breaking community — some celebrated unprecedented recognition + funding; others worried about the imposition of standardised + scored competition formats on a battle culture rooted in cypher + crew + on-the-spot improvisation. The B-girl Raygun (Rachael Gunn, Australia) incident — a non-canonical performance receiving viral mockery — opened a global debate on selection processes, gatekeeping + the gap between battle culture + Olympic infrastructure. Breaking will *not* return for LA 2028; the Olympic experiment is for now a single-edition phenomenon. Yet the Paris 2024 inclusion put breaking on prime-time global broadcast + accelerated state-funded breaking programmes in dozens of countries.

**Wayne McGregor + Random International**. **Wayne McGregor** (b.1970, UK; Resident Choreographer Royal Ballet from 2006; CBE) has been a 21C pioneer of **science + technology + choreography** fusion:
- Long-running collaboration with the Wellcome Trust + cognitive neuroscience laboratories — choreographing in dialogue with research on movement, memory, perception.
- **Mind + Movement / Living Archive** (with Google Arts & Culture, 2018-2023) — trained a machine-learning model on his own choreographic archive + uses it as a real-time generative collaborator in the studio.
- ***Atomos* (2013), *Autobiography* (2017), *Universal Connection* (2019), *MADDADDAM* (2022, Atwood novel), *UniVerse* (2023)*** — works integrating algorithmic processes into the studio practice.
- **Random International** (Hannes Koch + Florian Ortkrass, London-based art collective famous for *Rain Room* 2012) — collaborated with McGregor on **+/- Human** (2017) at the Roundhouse, in which dancers + airborne autonomous spheres performed together; live human-machine choreography for general audiences.
- The Mendeley + UCL **Choreographic Thinking Tools** project — formal capture of the cognitive operations McGregor's company uses (mirroring, transposing, augmenting, recombining) for use in interdisciplinary research + creative AI.

**Motion capture as choreographic + archival medium**. Vicon + OptiTrack optical mocap + Xsens + Rokoko inertial suits + markerless options (Theia, OpenPose) — recording rates of 60-240 Hz, joint precision ~1 mm. Choreographic uses:
- **Archive** — Cunningham Trust + Forsythe Company + Pite + McGregor archives include mocap.
- **Process** — choreographer captures studio improvisation + plays it back, edits, recomposes.
- **Transfer** — choreography moves between human dancer + animated avatar + robot + game character (P89 L4 cross-reference).
- **AI training data** — see next slide.

**Other major 21C technology-choreographers**: Klaus Obermaier (*Apparition* with Ars Electronica), OpenEndedGroup (with Cunningham), Marlene Monteiro Freitas (Cape Verde, Portugal), Boris Charmatz (Musée de la Danse). The 21C frontier has many groups working at the intersection of AI + dance + media art.

slides.title: AI choreography + Dance Diffuser + climate + global commissioning
slides.body:
**Generative AI applied to choreography** is the most actively-evolving frontier of the field in 2024-2026.

**Approaches**:
- **Sequence models on mocap data** — trained on motion-capture datasets (AIST++ , HumanML3D, MotionX), generate joint-trajectory sequences conditioned on music, text or seed motion. Examples: **EDGE** (Stanford 2022, Tseng + Castellon + Ren), **DanceFormer**, **Bailando** (2022, transformer + reinforcement learning).
- **Diffusion models for motion** — **MDM (Motion Diffusion Model)** (Tevet + Bermano 2022), **MoFusion**, **MotionGPT** (2023). The text 'do a backflip then a slow turn left' becomes a joint-trajectory sequence.
- ***Dance Diffuser*** (Google + Microsoft research lineage, 2023-2025) — a diffusion-based motion model conditioned on music + text + style, oriented to choreographic exploration rather than to dancer-replacement.
- **Google Arts & Culture *Living Archive*** (Wayne McGregor + Bill T. Jones precursor work) — a model trained on a choreographer's own archive that generates phrases in the choreographer's recognisable style. McGregor's 'Living Archive' is the canonical commercial-grade example (2018-2023).
- **AI as a *partner in the studio*** rather than a replacement — McGregor's working pattern. The model generates suggestions; the choreographer + dancers select, modify, ignore, recompose. The model is a stochastic improvisation partner.

**Open questions**:
- **Authorship + rights** — when the model trained on a choreographer's archive generates a new phrase, who owns it? Living Archive resolved this by treating the model as an extension of the choreographer + retaining their rights.
- **Cultural sensitivity** — models trained on Western mocap datasets default to balletic / contemporary forms; under-represent Bharatanatyam, Kathak, flamenco, African + Latino vernacular forms. The Bharatanatyam *mudra* + facial *abhinaya* are largely invisible to current mocap pipelines.
- **Replacement anxiety** — the dancer-as-labour question. So far, AI is amplifying the choreographer; it has not displaced the dancer. The body is the irreducible thing.
- **Quality + variety** — AI-generated motion is recognisably 'AI' (smoothed, mid-tempo, joint-physical) + struggles with the extremes (Forsythe-level off-balance attack, Bausch-level autobiographical specificity).

**Climate impact + dance**. Dance has a significant + under-discussed carbon footprint:
- **International touring** — passenger flights for a 30-person company on a 12-city European tour ~150 tCO₂e.
- **Sets + costumes** — production materials, freight.
- **Audience travel** — typically the largest single component for any concert form.
Response strategies emerging: **regional touring blocks** (rail-feasible); **digital + remote distribution** (filmed work, livestreams); **set-reuse + costume-reuse pledges** (UK's Theatre Green Book 2021); **co-commissioning** (multiple presenters share a single new work, distributing carbon + cost). Pina Bausch Foundation, the Royal Ballet, NDT have published climate strategies; the *Dance Artists' National Forum on Climate* (UK) + *EarthDance* (Boston) are organising sector responses.

**Global commissioning**. The 2020s have seen explicit decentralisation of choreographic commissioning away from a small NYC + Paris + London + Wuppertal canon:
- **Akram Khan + Akademi** (UK + global Kathak diaspora).
- **Hofesh Shechter + Israeli + diaspora networks**.
- **Crystal Pite + Kidd Pivot** (Vancouver — major Western co-commissions globally).
- **Camille A. Brown** (Black-American vernacular + concert).
- **Faye Driscoll** (NYC postmodern + immersive).
- **Marlene Monteiro Freitas** (Cabo Verde + Lisbon).
- **Eun-Me Ahn** (South Korea).
- **Rocío Molina + Israel Galván** (post-flamenco).
- **The Africa Centre + Dance Umbrella** + **South African + East African touring networks**.

The **2026 horizon** for the choreographer combines: a TikTok + Instagram + YouTube reality where dances spread without permission; an Olympic breaking moment now partially closed; AI as an in-studio collaborator; climate-aware programming + touring; an increasingly global + diasporic commissioning landscape. Every choreographer entering the field today must reason about all five at once.

question.question: Strategic plan for a mid-career choreographer in 2026
question.goal: You are a mid-career choreographer with an 8-dancer company, a strong UK + EU presenter network + a 5-year strategic plan to draft. Build the plan across the five frontiers — TikTok, AI, Olympic-era hip-hop infrastructure, climate, global commissioning.

steps.motivation: Use the platform without losing core craft.

acceptedAnswers: create a recurring 8-count studio hook series + credit + license dancers + treat platform as recruitment + reach but not core work

steps.reveal: Treat TikTok + Instagram as a *recruitment + reach + revenue* layer separate from concert practice. Post a recurring studio-hook series of 8-count phrases with full credit to the choreographers + dancers + a clear licensing policy; consider stitch / duet invitations to grow distribution. Do not let platform constraints (8-count hook, vertical, 60 s) shape your concert composition. Learn from the *Renegade* (Jalaiah Harmon) case + always credit the originating dancer.

steps.prompt: AI as in-studio collaborator — adopt or refuse?

acceptedAnswers: adopt as exploration tool; train on company's own archive (Living Archive pattern); never let AI generate final material

steps.reveal: Adopt AI as an exploration + ideation tool; follow the Wayne McGregor / Living Archive pattern. Train a model on the company's own motion-capture archive so the suggestions are in the company's recognisable style; treat outputs as *prompts* for human dancers to respond to, modify, refuse. Retain rights + authorship. Never present AI-generated motion as a finished work — the dance remains the body.

steps.prompt: Olympic-era hip-hop infrastructure — how do you intersect?

acceptedAnswers: commission a breaking + concert-dance hybrid; pay battle-credentialed dancers properly; respect cypher culture

steps.reveal: Commission a deliberate cross-genre hybrid work that engages with breaking + locking + popping vocabulary in a concert setting (cf. P89 L2 + L6). Cast battle-credentialed dancers at full company rates with credit; involve them in choreographic decisions; respect cypher culture's improvisation + lineage. Do not extract vocabulary without acknowledgement (a continuing failure mode in the concert sector). Paris 2024 grew the global infrastructure — use it ethically.

acceptedAnswers: regional touring blocks rail-feasible; co-commission with multiple presenters; reusable sets + costumes; UK Theatre Green Book

steps.reveal: Restructure touring into rail-feasible regional blocks (Continental EU or UK + Ireland or specific North American corridors) rather than transatlantic + intra-Asia patchwork. Co-commission with 3-5 presenters so a single new work amortises carbon + cost. Adopt the UK *Theatre Green Book* (2021) standards for set + costume reuse. Publish an annual climate report. Engage with the *Dance Artists' National Forum on Climate* + *EarthDance*.

steps.prompt: Global commissioning — where do you build relationships?

acceptedAnswers: build long-term relationships with non-canon presenters — African + South Asian + Latin American festivals + diaspora networks

steps.reveal: Invest in long-term, multi-year relationships with non-canonical presenters — South African + East African festivals (Dance Umbrella Johannesburg, Sauti za Busara), South Asian Kathak + Bharatanatyam diaspora networks (Akademi, Bharat Bhavan), Latin American + Caribbean festivals, Pacific + Indigenous presenters. Avoid one-off tokenist commissioning. Pair with local co-choreographers; share authorial credit. The 2020s decentralisation of choreography is a generational opportunity.

question.question: What did the *Renegade* case (2019-2020) reveal about TikTok + viral choreography?
options: Jalaiah Harmon (14, Atlanta) created the *Renegade* choreography to K Camp's *Lottery* in September 2019 + posted it to Funimate + Instagram. The dance spread to TikTok where Charli D'Amelio (15) posted it without credit + accumulated ~100M views; Harmon went uncredited as the choreographer for months + did not benefit financially from the virality. The *New York Times* story (February 2020, Taylor Lorenz) made *Renegade* the canonical case of uncredited Black creators of viral choreography. It revealed: (1) algorithmic platforms decouple choreography from author + from compensation; (2) credit + compensation systems do not exist for viral dance the way they do for music; (3) Black + Latino vernacular dance circulates uncredited; (4) reform is slow + driven by external press + industry pressure. The case shaped subsequent practice (e.g. Brian Esperon credited for *WAP* 2020) + remains the reference case for industry conversations on credit.
Choreographers always get rich from viral fame.
TikTok has formal credit attribution baked in.
question.explanation: *Renegade* (2019-2020) revealed TikTok virality systematically uncredits + uncompensates choreographers, especially Black + Latino vernacular creators. Jalaiah Harmon created the dance + went uncredited while Charli D'Amelio's version went to ~100M views; the *NYT* Lorenz story (Feb 2020) made it the canonical case + drove modest industry reform.

What did the NYT story expose?

question.question: An AI-collaboration commission
question.prompt: A major museum + a tech company offer your company a $2M, 18-month commission to make a 60-minute evening-length work that integrates AI as a visible part of the creative + performance process. The brief asks for: (a) a model trained on your past archive; (b) on-stage interaction between dancers + machine-generated material; (c) public outputs (talks, a film, a downloadable model). Outline (1) your ethical conditions before accepting (training data consent, rights, dancer pay, climate impact of compute, refusal options); (2) your studio process — how AI enters + at what stage; (3) what the audience actually sees of the AI on stage + what stays invisible; (4) the dramaturgical risk you have to manage so the work is more than a tech demo.

question.question: A motion-capture archive contains 200 hours of recording at 120 Hz with 30 joints × 3 coordinates × 4-byte floats. Compute the total uncompressed data volume in gigabytes (1 GB = 10⁹ bytes). Round to one decimal.

question.prompt: In ≤160 words, name the five frontier pressures on a 2026 choreographer + explain how a mid-career artist can engage each ethically. Reference the *Renegade* case, Paris 2024 breaking, Wayne McGregor + Living Archive, climate + global commissioning.
question.rubric: Should name + address: (1) **viral platforms** — TikTok + Instagram decouple choreography from author (*Renegade* / Jalaiah Harmon / Charli D'Amelio 2019-2020; *WAP* / Brian Esperon 2020). Engagement: post + credit + license; treat platform as reach not core work. (2) **Olympic-era hip-hop infrastructure** — Paris 2024 breaking (Ami + Phil Wizard gold), now LA 2028 excluded. Engagement: cross-genre commissioning with battle-credentialed dancers + cypher culture respect. (3) **AI choreography** — Wayne McGregor + Random International + Google Living Archive; EDGE + MDM + Dance Diffuser. Engagement: use AI as in-studio partner trained on own archive; rights retained; never replace dancer. (4) **Climate** — international touring is the field's largest carbon footprint. Engagement: regional rail-feasible blocks, co-commissioning, reusable sets, Theatre Green Book standards. (5) **Global commissioning** — decentralisation away from NYC + Paris + London canon. Engagement: long-term relationships with African + South Asian + Latin American + diaspora presenters; co-authorial credit. The 2026 choreographer reasons about all five simultaneously.
